text.tspan: Figure 5. Principal component 1 (PC1), the “elongate–globose” spore shape axis, in relation to precipitation and climate. (A) We analyzed mean PC1 by species
as a function of precipitation during the 30 days prior to collection of each species’ holotype (r=-0.37, p=0.0087). (B) We analyzed mean PC1 by species as a
Köppen Climate Groups based on the location the holotype was found (p=0.03174). To account for the fact that closely related species may resemble
one another because of shared evolutionary history, we also fit phylogenetic generalized least squares (PGLS) models on the subset of species for which
phylogenetic data were available. We compared three models predicting PC1 from (1) precipitation, (2) climate group, and (3) both predictors using Akaike’s
Information Criterion corrected for small sample size (AICc). The model including precipitation alone received the strongest support (R²=.24, p=0.0202), whereas
climate group did not explain additional variation once precipitation was included.
